rubrics.justification: Accurately identifies a blastocoel, intact zona, probable right-sided ICM, and somewhat uneven TE, and correctly notes inconsistency between image and reported 2AA/full-blast description. Minor overcalling of ICM/TE quality from a single still image prevents a perfect score.
Comprehensively integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, unexplained infertility, endometrium, semen parameters, first-cycle status, and transfer timing with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, with probability estimates tied to embryo quality and patient factors. Small uncertainty arises from discussing a day-4 blastocyst using day-5 style implantation expectations and from some speculative fresh-transfer receptivity concerns without hormone data.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with Gardner grading principles, SET in a young good-prognosis patient, luteal support, and avoiding routine PGT-A at age 27. Slight downgrade because some comments on fresh-transfer physiology/OHSS and day-4 interpretation are reasonable but not tightly guideline-based.

Provides clear practical next steps: proceed with SET, ensure luteal support, monitor for OHSS symptoms, optimize peri-transfer lifestyle, and outlines sensible future-cycle contingencies including cohort review, grading clarification, possible FET strategy, and selective male-factor workup.
